first_3_seconds: He stands in front of a silver Ram holding a huge polished fan-shaped exhaust tip against his chest, white text box on top, then a quick cut to him crouched holding it up to the rear bumper.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Putting BOOM TUBES On My Diesel Truck". Spoken: "I'm putting boom tubes on my diesel truck."
why_it_went_viral: 182x his median but only 0.08 percent shares, so this was pushed by watch time and a live trend, not by sends: an odd shiny object in frame at second zero, a trend borrowed from car TikTok (stitched clip of the car creator), and a claim to be first on a diesel. It never delivers the sound (turbo is dead), which kept people watching and arguing in comments.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Barely shared. The few sends are truck guys to a buddy with "look what they are doing now".
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Hold the strange part in frame from the first frame, say in one line what you are about to do with it, explain what it is, and end on an open promise of the result.

first_3_seconds: Split screen: top half is footage of a well-known truck YouTuber being walked in handcuffs by an officer, bottom half is Zac's face close to a small fuzzy mic, text box across the middle.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Whistlindiesel Has Been Arrested For Tax Evasion". Spoken: "WhistlinDiesel has been arrested for tax evasion."
why_it_went_viral: 45x median. He was early on breaking news about the biggest name in the truck world, and the arrest footage is on screen the whole time while he explains the Montana plate angle in plain words. Shares are modest (0.34 percent); it rode search and curiosity.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Truck and car guys to the group chat: "did you see this".
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: News desk: the source clip on the top half, your face and a mic on the bottom half, headline as the first sentence, then what happened and what it means for a regular owner, in 60 seconds.

first_3_seconds: POV hands shake a green spray can and point it at the license plate on a Super Duty bumper, then hold the can label up to the lens.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Protecting My License Plate From Flock Cameras". Spoken: "I'm going to show you how to protect the license plate on your truck from Flock cameras using this."
why_it_went_viral: 43x median with 36,500 shares (1.59 percent). A cheap hardware-store can aimed at a thing a lot of drivers resent (plate reader cameras), plus scarcity: "get it before they stop selling it" and the store clerk story at the end. The topic reaches far past truck people.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Anyone who distrusts the cameras, to friends and family who drive: "go get a can".
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: One cheap off-the-shelf product, shown in hand in the first second, solving a thing drivers are annoyed by, with the exact product name said out loud. Skip the plate trick itself: covering or altering a plate is illegal in most states.

first_3_seconds: He crouches at the back of a lifted Super Duty and points at a giant flat exhaust tip sticking out under the bumper, text box on top, then cuts to him walking up holding the part.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "How To Install BOOM TUBES". Spoken: "We finally have the boom tubes on the truck."
why_it_went_viral: 30x median, 0.05 percent shares. It is the payoff episode to the 9.8M video, so the audience was already waiting, and the result looks ridiculous on purpose. Views came from the series and comments, not sends.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Almost nobody shares it. It is a follow-along for people who saw part one.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Part two of a promise: open on the finished thing already on the truck, then rewind and show the install in quick POV steps.

first_3_seconds: He stands next to a silver Ram holding a long white PVC pipe upright like a staff and points at it, text box on top, then a clip of another creator's truck with PVC bars.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Making PVC Traction Bars". Spoken: "Thanks to PVC traction bars." (shouts out the guy who did it first, "this is going to save me a bunch of money")
why_it_went_viral: 26x median. A deliberately dumb budget build played completely straight: a 70 dollar PVC copy of a part that costs many hundreds. Half the viewers laugh, half get mad and comment that it does nothing, and both groups feed it.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Truck guys to the buddy who overspends on parts, or to the buddy who would actually do this.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Build the cheap fake version of an expensive part with a straight face, step by step in POV, and end on the price.

first_3_seconds: He crouches at the hitch of a Ram holding a bag of zip ties, a red tow strap lying on the ground, text box on top.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Diesel Truck vs Zipties". Spoken: "How many zip ties does it take to stop my truck?"
why_it_went_viral: 26x median but 0.02 percent shares. A pure curiosity test with a counting ladder (1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 75) and a visible snap each round, so people stay to see the number where it holds. Watch time carried it; nobody sends it.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Hardly anyone. It is a watch-to-the-end video, not a send.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: One question in the first sentence, then an escalating count with the same locked-off camera angle each round, so the only thing that changes is the number.

first_3_seconds: Top half: a truck rolling coal on a road. Bottom half: his face close to a mic. Text box across the middle. At 3 seconds it cuts to a White House press clip.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "ITS LEGAL TO DELETE DIESELS AGAIN (With Proof)". Spoken: "Breaking news. The Clean Air Act will no longer be enforced."
why_it_went_viral: 22x median with 29,700 shares (2.48 percent). It tells diesel owners the thing they most want to hear and shows official footage as proof. Note the claim is overstated (dropping criminal cases is not the same as deleting being legal), and that overstatement is a big part of why it traveled.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Every diesel owner to every other diesel owner, and to the buddy who got fined or is scared to delete.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Good-news-for-owners bulletin: the official clip first, then your face saying what changed and what did not, in plain words. Jacob can be the one who gets it right.

first_3_seconds: He is lying on his side on the driveway under a silver Ram wrestling an orange traction bar, text box on top, then a close shot of fresh drilled holes in the frame.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Traction Bar Install DIDN'T End Well". Spoken: "I don't know how, but I found a way to mess up a bolt-on installation."
why_it_went_viral: 18x median, 0.03 percent shares. He admits the failure up front and asks for help in the caption, which pulls a flood of advice and roasting comments. It also calls back to the PVC bars. Comment bait through honesty, not a send.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Rarely shared. People comment instead: the ones who know how to set a rivnut.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Open with the mistake already made and shown on camera, rewind through how it happened, end on the real question you need answered.

first_3_seconds: A photo of a two-tone brown and tan Ford Taurus fills the top, his cut-out face in a bucket hat talks in the lower corner on black, text box on top.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "King Ranch Taurus is Straight Aura". Spoken: "I've seen a King Ranch F250, but have you seen a King Ranch Ford Taurus?"
why_it_went_viral: 17x median with 25,000 shares (2.81 percent, his best send rate). An odd find everyone can judge in one second, compared side by side with the truck it copies, and it ends on a simple yes or no question.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Ford guys to each other, and to the buddy with a King Ranch: "you need the matching car".
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: React to one weird vehicle photo: "you have seen X, but have you seen Y", show the photo, compare it to the truck people know, ask would you buy it.

first_3_seconds: Top half: a graphic of three diesel engines under "R.I.P." (6.7 Cummins, L5P Duramax, Power Stroke). Bottom half: his face at a mic. Then engine bay photos swap in as he names each one.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "2027 Is The End of a Era For Modern Diesels". Spoken: "2027 will be the end of an era for modern-day diesels as we know it."
why_it_went_viral: 16x median with 17,200 shares (1.94 percent). An end-of-an-era headline that covers all three brands, so every camp has a stake, with spec numbers on screen for each. The claims are thinly sourced, which also drives arguing in comments.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Brand loyalists to their rival-brand buddy, and owners to the buddy about to buy a new truck.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Three-brand rundown: one big claim, then Ford, Ram and GM each get 15 seconds with a photo and two numbers on screen. Only with numbers he can back up.

first_3_seconds: Low-angle selfie by an open truck door, bearded guy talking to himself about putting on a hoodie, small text box on top. At 3 seconds it cuts to the same guy in red wraparound shades as a second character.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Carhartt gatekeepers be like". Spoken: "Getting chilly out, better grab the Carhartt sweater." / "Carhartt? He must have served. Where were you deployed?"
why_it_went_viral: 23x median. A two-character skit that names a brand nearly everyone owns and a guy everyone has met, pushed to absurd (stolen valor for a hoodie). People tag whoever wears Carhartt without doing trade work.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Tradesmen to the office friend in a Carhartt, and the office friend back to the tradesman.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: One man, two characters: normal guy says an innocent line, cut to the same man in sunglasses overreacting. Same low angle, sunglasses are the whole costume.

first_3_seconds: Low-angle indoor selfie, bald bearded guy says his salary to the room. At 3 seconds it cuts to him in purple shield glasses facing the other way.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Welders for no reason". Spoken: "You know, I didn't do too bad this year. I made about 85,000." / "85,000? What's it like living below the poverty line, cupcake?"
why_it_went_viral: 22x median. It roasts one specific trade for bragging about money and the truck, with quotable insults ("cupcake", "don't even fill up the Duramax"). Everyone knows that welder.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Every trade to the welder they know, and welders to each other.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: [Group] for no reason title, then the calm guy states a normal fact and the sunglasses character one-ups it until it gets ridiculous.

first_3_seconds: Outdoor low-angle selfie in falling snow, guy in a gray beanie looks up and remarks on the weather. At 3 seconds, same guy in pink shades answers.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "When you complain about the weather around a blue collar guy". Spoken: "Geez, this weather sure is nasty." / "Try working in it, buddy. 168 hour shifts. You'd fold like a lawn chair."
why_it_went_viral: 22x median. A universal small-talk moment met with a line every outdoor worker has said or heard, and posted while it was actually snowing. The "168 hours" bit is his running joke.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Wives and coworkers to the blue collar guy who says exactly this, and tradesmen to each other.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Take one everyday sentence people say to you and answer it as the over-the-top tough guy, filmed outside in the actual weather.

first_3_seconds: Low-angle indoor selfie, bald bearded guy asks about base model trucks. At 4 seconds he cuts to himself in dark shades as the salesman.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Buying a truck in 2025 be like". Spoken: "What do you guys have for base models? You know, just cloth interior, nothing fancy."
why_it_went_viral: 20x median but a low 0.15 percent shares. Truck prices are a sore spot for every buyer, and the 57,000 dollar base model line lands as the punch. It was watched and agreed with more than it was sent.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Guys shopping for a truck to the buddy who just bought one, or to dad: "this is why I am keeping the old one".
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Buyer and salesman, both played by him: a reasonable ask, then one real price delivered deadpan as the punchline.

first_3_seconds: Low-angle indoor selfie, guy stretches and says he has to get to bed. At 3 seconds, same guy in black shield shades cuts in.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Concrete guys be like". Spoken: "Geez, I better get to bed. I've got to be up at 5 a.m." / "Cupcake. I'm already on my fifth coffee by 5 a.m."
why_it_went_viral: 20x median. Trade-specific bragging (up earlier, works alone, Duramax lit up like a stadium) that ends with the truck not being paid off. The roasted trade shares it proudly.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Concrete guys to their crew, and other trades to the concrete guy they know.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: [Trade] guys be like: the normal guy sets up with a plain line, the character tops it three times, and the last line undercuts him.

first_3_seconds: Low-angle indoor selfie, guy in dark shades already mid-complaint. Text box on top. At 5 seconds the calm version of him answers.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Blue collar finances". Spoken: "I mean, I'm working 168 hours a day and I barely have enough money to eat." / "I thought you make like 45 bucks an hour."
why_it_went_viral: 19x median. The truck payment joke: good wage, broke anyway because of an 1,100 dollar Duramax payment, Zyns, energy drinks, a boat and a side-by-side. It stings because it is true for a lot of viewers.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Wives and girlfriends to the guy with the truck payment, and buddies to the one with the newest truck.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Calm guy asks simple money questions, the character lists his expenses one short item at a time, each one worse.

first_3_seconds: Low-angle indoor shot of him looking into an open shoebox with new sneakers. At 3 seconds, same guy in orange shades cuts in.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Blue collar guys for no reason". Spoken: "Oh yeah, new pair of Jordans, these things are clean." / "Flexin' a 100 dollar pair of Jordans, cupcake. My work boots start at 500."
why_it_went_viral: 19x median with 54,200 shares. A prop in the first second and a familiar one-upper: whatever you bought, his work gear cost more and gets destroyed faster. Ends on the gas truck dig.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Friends and partners to the tradesman who turns everything into how hard he works.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Start with a prop in hand and one happy line, then the character turns it into a contest about work.

first_3_seconds: Low-angle outdoor selfie under a porch roof, bald bearded guy politely asks to renew his license. At 3 seconds, same guy in blue mirrored shades as the clerk.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "DMV employees be like". Spoken: "I was just wondering if I could renew my driver's license, please." / "Do you have an original copy of the Treaty of Versailles, Declaration of Independence and the Bill of Rights?"
why_it_went_viral: 18x median with 70,100 shares (1.52 percent). Not a trades joke at all: everybody has been through the DMV, so the audience is the whole country, and the document list escalates to an umbilical cord.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Anyone to anyone who just went to the DMV, especially family.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Pick a counter everyone has stood at, play the customer straight and the clerk asking for more and more absurd things.

first_3_seconds: Low-angle outdoor selfie against a cloudy sky, guy in a tan Carhartt cap as the boss starts an interview. At 5 seconds, same guy without the cap answers.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Blue collar interview (concrete version)". Spoken: "The job is just concrete laborer, so just tell me a little about yourself and why I should hire you."
why_it_went_viral: 17x median. A job interview turned upside down: every red flag (three divorces, child support, Duramax payment, lives at the Motel 6) makes him "overqualified". Crews recognize the guy.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Crew members to the boss and to each other: "this is our new hire".
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Interview format with a hat as the only costume change: the boss asks a normal question, the applicant answers with flaws that the boss treats as strengths.

first_3_seconds: Low-angle outdoor selfie under a bright blue sky, guy tilts his head back and says it is hot. At 2 seconds, same guy in red shield shades leans in.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "When you mention the weather around a blue collar guy". Spoken: "It is hot out, my goodness." / "Why don't you try working in it, brother. 168 hours a week."
why_it_went_viral: 16x median but his best send rate: 107,800 shares (2.63 percent). It is the summer remake of the snow skit, posted in a heat wave, with a fresh bit (hot Gatorade, no time to collect ice). Proof that a working premise can be reshot by season.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Partners and office coworkers to the outdoor worker, and tradesmen to their crew in the heat.
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Reshoot a skit that already worked with one variable changed (season, weather, place), same title pattern and same character.
